Girls Garden
Field Manual

Everything the Japanese strategy wikis document about how マブラヴ ガールズガーデン actually works — formation maths, the limit-break trap, verified affinity gains, the daily loop, and the three walls that stop everyone. Consolidated into one reference, in English.

Read First Combat Attributes Status Growth Affinity Maze Modes Daily Gacha Walls Tier Board Choices Sources All
The short version

Six things that decide everything

The game explains almost none of this — a complaint that recurs in every Japanese guide. If you read nothing else, read these.

Trap

Never limit-break R and SR characters

Once a character reaches LR, limit break stops needing same-name style cards and accepts any card of the same attribute. That makes your junk R/SR cards the shared currency for pushing SSRs to LR. Spend them on the low-rarity characters themselves and you burn the resource you'll need later. As one guide puts it: 「低レアは重ねるな。スタイルカードは余らないぞ！」

Structural

You need five 4★-broken SSRs

An un-limit-broken character caps at level 160, which is not enough for later content. The design assumes limit breaks; the walls are tuned for it. Five limit-broken SSRs is the real mid-game target, and Level Link then carries the rest of your roster.

Free power

Match all five attributes

A full five-of-one-attribute team grants +25% ATK and +25% HP. That is larger than most upgrades you can buy, it costs nothing, and auto-formation will not do it for you — auto tends to scatter attributes. Calculator below.

Free power

Respect the rows

Every character has a preferred row. Put a front-row unit in the back and she takes −5% to HP, ATK and DEF. It's small per character and quietly compounds across a party of five.

Underrated

Affinity is a stat system

Not just story unlocks. Maxing affinity (Lv 40) was measured at +3,156 HP, +2,383 ATK, +1,302 DEF — flat values, so proportionally enormous early. Five daily interactions, and they're free.

Timing

Reset is 05:00 JST

That is 20:00 UTC the previous day — 22:00 the previous evening at UTC+2, 21:00 at UTC+1, 15:00 at UTC−5. Outside East Asia your "daily" tasks roll over during your evening rather than overnight, so a day's five-attempt allowances can expire while you still think of it as today.

Formation

Combat and the five slots

Combat is fully automatic. Every decision you make happens before you press start, which makes formation the entire skill expression of the game.

The party

  • Five characters, split across 前衛 Vanguard (front row) and 後衛 Rearguard (back row)
  • Each has a suitable position; some are flagged as suitable for both
  • Wrong row = −5% HP, ATK and DEF
  • A sixth slot appears in some high-difficulty content
  • Battles run themselves — up to 3× speed plus skip

Types and roles

Three types — 物理 Physical · EN Energy · 敏捷 Agile. These drive the Maze チューンナップ upgrades, which are applied per type.

Five roles. A workable core is one tank, two attackers, one support, one control, all sharing an attribute.

Physical Attacker物理アタッカー
EN AttackerENアタッカー
Tankタンク
Supportサポート
Controlコントロール

A 3+2 split gives the same ATK as a 4-stack but 5% less HP, so a 4+1 is worth building toward once you have the units. The jump from 4 to 5 matching is the biggest single step in the table.

Six attributes

The 四竦み and the two outside it

In the cycle

アグレッシブ Aggressive · スマート Smart · シャイ Shy · キュート Cute

Outside it

クレバー Clever · コミカル Comical

Advantage

+25% damage attacking into a disadvantaged attribute; being disadvantaged halves your damage

Why Clever characters are rated so highly Four attributes sit in a 四竦み — a four-way standoff where each beats one and loses to another. クレバー sits outside that cycle, so nothing halves it. That universal consistency is the main reason 榊野ヒイロ tops the tier lists: she never has a bad matchup. The trade is availability — Clever and Comical units have notoriously low drop rates, which makes limit-breaking them a long project.

The cycle, resolved

Earlier versions of this manual flagged the direction as unverified. It is now documented: Shy → Cute → Smart → Aggressive → Shy, where the arrow means "beats". Colours are the ones the game uses on card badges.

シャイ Shy ▶ キュート Cute ▶ スマート Smart ▶ アグレッシブ Aggressive ▶ back to Shy
Smart スマート
beatsAggressive
loses toCute
Aggressive アグレッシブ
beatsShy
loses toSmart
Shy シャイ
beatsCute
loses toAggressive

beatsSmart
loses toShy

beatsComical only

What this changes in practice Clever and Comical are a closed pair — they have advantage only against each other, and the four-colour cycle cannot touch them either way. So the "nothing halves Clever" line above holds for all ordinary content, and it also means a Comical unit is the one thing that punishes a Clever-heavy enemy team. Separately: the wishlist gives the four cycle attributes 4 slots each but Comical and Clever only 1 each, so you can aim at a Clever unit — just not at more than one of them at a time. Combined with drop rates reported around 0.02%, that is why finishing 榊野ヒイロ or ドロテア is a lifetime project.
状態異常

Status effects, and who inflicts them

The game's own term is 状態異常, which the official English renders as status ailment; the effect names below are the official ones too, taken from the translated skill text. Seven exist. Two of them — stun and freeze — simply delete an enemy's turn, which is worth more than any damage buff in the five-turn formats. Because combat is automatic, the only way to "play around" an enemy is to bring the right debuffer, so this table is the closest thing the game has to a counter-pick list.

気絶 Stun14 sources — the most common

The target can use no active, passive or extra skill, and burns AP and EX gauge when her turn comes round anyway. A stunned unit does not merely skip — she pays for skipping.

榊野ヒイロドロテア・カークランドエヴィ・レーナルト桃園める Meruリリー・ラヴォア Lilyリュシー・ムーアクロフト御剣冥夜鳴滝七彩 Narutaki月ヶ瀬ちゆる Chiyuru生駒葵綺羅クララ榊千鶴ライブシエナナージャ・ヴォルコワ

炎上 Burn9 sources

Fixed damage each time the target acts, scaled off the inflictor's attack stat — not the target's HP. That makes burn best on a high-ATK unit and reliable against low-HP enemies, and it keeps working through defence buffs.

ユリア・バーンズ紫雲沙耶フィー・ドレーゼノエル・アルエ Noelleレイヴェル・ブライトリーフ鳴滝七彩 Narutaki姫川泉花ジュリー・ステイシー Julie黒森ラウラ Laura

毒 Poison3 sources

Damage as a percentage of the target's current HP each time she acts. The mirror image of burn: useless for finishing something off, outstanding against high-HP bosses where flat numbers stop mattering. Bring poison to the Maze, burn to the ladder.

アニス・ベネット月ヶ瀬ちゆる Chiyuruハリエット・ミルズ Harriette

凍結 Freeze4 sources

Blocks skills like stun, with two differences that matter: a charging skill is not cancelled, it just waits — and dealing damage to a frozen target removes the freeze. So freeze is a lockdown you can accidentally break yourself. Freeze the target you are not attacking.

鳴滝七彩 Narutaki朽葉ラミ Ramiケイト・フルニエ Kateミリアム・ヘイワード Miriam

暗闇 Blind1 source

Skills fail to land on a probability — and notably it overrides 必中 Sure Hit buffs, which nothing else in the game does. A niche answer to one specific enemy archetype.

ステラ・ブレーメル

混乱 Confusion1 source

The target's attacking skills hit her own side instead. In a five-turn format, turning an enemy attacker on her own tank is the single largest tempo swing available.

オルガ・ヴォルコワ

幻惑 Illusionno documented source yet

Strips every non-damage effect from the target's active skills and converts her damage into healing for whoever she hits. Listed in the game's own effect glossary but no character on the wiki is recorded as applying it — likely reserved for enemies or an unreleased unit.

Freeze relics in the Maze will undo your own lock This connects to the trap-relic warning further down: some Maze relics remove freeze effects, including yours. If your run is built around 凍結, read every relic before taking it.
Investment

Growth, and where to spend

Five separate upgrade tracks compete for the same limited materials. The Japanese wikis broadly agree on this ordering.

★★★
Character level
The single biggest and cheapest power gain. Fuelled by トレーニングレポート and funds from idle rewards. Do this before anything else.
★★☆
Maze tune-up チューンナップ · Affinity 親愛度
Both are slow-drip, permanent and free. Tune-up upgrades whole types at once; affinity adds flat stats to individuals.
★☆☆
Skill enhancement · Module enhancement
Skill levels need スキルレポート from the Maze; modules add flat HP/ATK/DEF. Worth doing, not worth rushing.
Last
Limit break 限界突破
Powerful but material-hungry, and the easiest place to waste resources permanently. Read the trap below before touching it.
This ordering is not one wiki's opinion gamerch's beginner page arrives at the same ranking independently — level ★★★, then Maze and affinity ★★☆, then skills and modules ★☆☆ — and closes with the same warning about not limit-breaking low-rarity cards. Two details it adds: module enhancement has a daily attempt limit, so it is a habit rather than a push, and its materials come from Tactical Exercise, which is the practical reason to clear those daily even when you cannot place in the rankings.
資金 is the quiet bottleneck, and mining is the whole answer Funds are consumed by character levels and module enhancement, and the cost per level grows steeply — so the resource that gates the ★★★ track is money, not training reports. Nearly all of it comes from mining, which accrues on a timer whether or not you are playing, and whose rate is set by your mining level. Mining level rises as you clear Battle Simulation stages, which rise as you advance the main quest. That is the actual engine of the game: main quest → simulate floors → mining level → funds → levels → main quest. Event exchanges occasionally offer unlimited funds; the advice is still to spend event currency on gacha tickets and memory pieces first, because funds regenerate on their own and those do not.

Level Link レベルリンク

Your five highest-level characters set a shared floor: the whole linked group is pulled up to the lowest level among those five. Practically, you pour everything into five units and the rest of your roster rides along free.

This is why the guides say to concentrate on one or two SSRs early rather than spreading levels around — and why the five you pick should be the five with the highest limit-break ceilings.

The rarity ladder

Limit breaking does not just raise a cap — it changes the card's rarity. That is why your box shows SR+, SSR+ and UR: those are limit-broken cards, not different pulls. These are the game's own emblems; the number below each is how many breaks it took.

Fourteen steps, thirteen breaks. An earlier revision of this manual started the ladder at SSR and missed the R+ and SR+ rungs; the emblem set shows low-rarity cards climb the same way. Level caps rise with it — 160 unbroken, then 170 / 180 / 190, reaching 200 at LR.

  • Skill level cap 15 is reached only through limit breaking
  • Past level 200, the Over Limit system locks in five characters; additional slots cost 500 gems each
The limit-break trap — the most expensive mistake available Pulling a student you already own does not give you a second copy. The game's own gacha text says so: 「すでに所持している生徒を獲得した場合、スタイルカードに変換されます。スタイルカードは、生徒の限界突破に使用します」 — a duplicate becomes a style card, and style cards are what limit breaking eats. Every style card in the data is tied to one specific card (桃園める［シリウスシュガーのエース］のスタイルカード), described simply as 「生徒の限界突破に必要なアイテム」.
StepWhat it costsWhose cards
R → SR10同名 — her own
SR+ → SSR20同名 — her own
SSR+ → UR+50同名 — her own
LR and beyond50 + 50同属性 — any card of that attribute
That inversion is the whole game. Up to UR+ a card can only be fed her own duplicates. From the LR step onward the requirement switches to 同属性 — the attribute pool — so every spare R and SR card of the right colour becomes fuel for finishing an SSR. Spend those on the R and SR characters themselves and they are gone. The conversion rates make the arithmetic brutal: one duplicate SSR is worth 50 cards, an SR 5, an R 1. Limit-breaking one R costs ten R duplicates — a tenth of an LR step, spent on a unit that will never carry you. Hoard low-rarity cards. Do not "just upgrade" that spare SR.
How far this one is verified Checked in September 2026 against three things. The game's own MasterData confirms the duplicate→style-card conversion, that style cards exist per individual card rather than as a generic currency, and that the rarity ladder really does run through LR and on to LR+1 … LR+5 (the mission text reads 「いずれかの生徒のレアリティをLR+5にする」). kamigame supplies the material table above, including the 同名 → 同属性 switch at LR and the 50 + 50 figure. A player blog independently reaches the same conclusion and adds the 50 / 5 / 1 conversion rates, with the same warning about low-rarity limit breaks.

What I could not confirm from the game files: the numbers themselves. The translation project's MasterData carries text fields only, so cost values are not in it, and the exact step at which 10 becomes 20 becomes 50 is a summary of kamigame's table rather than a quotation of it. Treat the rule as solid and the individual figures as a good secondary source. Nothing in the game data contradicts any of it — there is no generic "attribute style card" item, but the LR rule does not need one; the limit-break screen simply widens which cards it will accept.
親愛度

Affinity — the stat system disguised as romance

Verified gains at max (Lv 6 → 40)

StatMeasuredEst. total
HP+2,951+3,156
ATK+2,228+2,383
DEF+1,217+1,302

Roughly +5–10% ATK for a level-200 character. Crucially these are flat values, not percentages — so at low level they're proportionally far larger. Affinity is an early-game accelerant, not an endgame luxury.

How to raise it

  • Gifts — ギフトカード from daily and weekly missions. Collect every day; they're hard to bulk-farm
  • 学園スポット dates — unlocked at main quest 1-11, 5 per day
  • 待ち合わせ Meetup — designate up to 3 characters to appear the next day, so you aren't at the mercy of the rotation

Each campus guarantees at least 6 characters appearing, so you only need appointments for a campus where you own 7+.

The dates are not random, and there's a table Which event fires is determined by the character + spot combination, and each event has a choice that produces デート大成功 — "date great success", the better affinity outcome. A community wiki documents every pairing with the correct choice in bold: muvluvggkm.gamewiki.jp — 学園スポット. This is the one place where picking the "right" dialogue option measurably matters.

Affinity 10 → a dedicated Memory

Every character who is natively SSR grants a character-specific メモリー at affinity 10. These are strong and tuned to her kit. If you field two copies of the same character, the Memory's effect applies to both.

Maxing no longer locks you out

Reaching the Lv 40 cap once prevented you from seeing further date events with that character. That restriction was removed in an update, so there's no longer a reason to hold back.

メモリー

Memories — the reward affinity is actually for

Equipment, but you cannot buy or farm most of it: memories are unlocked by affinity, which makes the date loop an equipment pipeline rather than a side activity.

How they work

  • Two effects each. Effect 1 fires at battle start and buffs the wearer; effect 2 is a team-wide or conditional buff
  • 「メモリーはSSRキャラしか実装されていません」 — only natively-SSR characters have one. Your R and SR units have no memory to unlock, however much you date them
  • Character memories unlock from affinity 10
  • Team memories unlock at a combined affinity across that squad — between 27 and 45 depending on the team
  • Some also arrive through login bonuses and paid packs

Where to put them

「攻撃力のほうが重要なので、アタッカーのメモリーを優先して装備しましょう」 — attack outweighs everything else, so equip your attackers first and work outward. A defensive memory on a tank is close to wasted while an attacker is going without.

Team memories are a Maze tool. Their buffs are percentage-based, so they scale with investment and pay off in long multi-battle runs rather than in a single five-turn fight.

Two copies, two beneficiariesIf you field the same character twice, her memory's effect applies to both — one of the few places duplicates pay off outside limit breaks.

メイズ探索

Maze Exploration

Unlocks at main quest 1-13. Free to run, no stamina cost, and the standard answer whenever the main quest stops moving.

How a run works

  • Layer-clearing structure — several to about 10 consecutive battles
  • You pick a direction at each step; a boss waits on the deepest stratum
  • After each battle you choose a relic レリック, which shapes the next fight
  • Mining yields タツミヤ鉱 Tatsumiya ore, the run's main currency
  • A hidden merchant at depth 10 trades ore for relics
  • A harder 未開拓メイズ (Unexplored Maze) tier opens later

Spend ore in this order

1
Mining 採掘
Raises your passive income permanently, and that income feeds every other track. gamerch rates this ★★★, above everything else in the tune-up menu
2
Type equipment · Daily shop
Equipment lifts Physical / EN / Agile across your whole roster at once; the shop unlock lets you buy スキルレポート daily, which is otherwise the bottleneck on skill levels
3
Artifacts アーティファクト
Maze-only stats. Lowest return until you are deep enough for it to matter

Ore does not carry over

「タツミヤ鉱は持ち越しできない」 — whatever you are holding when the run ends is destroyed. Spend down to zero before you finish, even on something mediocre. This is the single most common way to waste a Maze run.

Upgrade caps rise every 10 floors

You cannot pour ore into one track indefinitely — each tune-up has a ceiling that lifts per 10 cleared floors. Depth is therefore the gate on everything, which is a second reason to push floors rather than farm a comfortable one.

Levels are capped at commander level

「生徒のレベルが指揮官レベルまでに制限される」 — inside the Maze your characters are clamped to your account level. Over-levelling one carry will not brute-force depth here the way it does the main quest.

Bonus characters, +5% to +20%

Each rotation flags bonus characters; fielding them scales ore gain from +5% for one up to +20% for all five. Check the banner before a long run — it is a free fifth of the run's income.

Watch for trap relics Not every relic is an upgrade. Players clearing the Unexplored Maze report 罠レリック — relics that undo a status you were relying on, notably ones that remove your own freeze effects. Read what a relic does before taking it; a good run can be thrown away by one careless pick.

チューンナップ is applied at the end of a run and upgrades an entire type — Physical, EN or Agile — at once. Individually small, but it lifts every character of that type simultaneously, which is why the guides rank it just behind raw levelling.

Route selection ルート選択

Every area deals a fresh set of nodes and you pick one. Two of the five choices are not available on a new account — the game unlocks them from play, and the triggers are in its own data:

Numbers are the value at the highest step each relic reaches, straight from the game's relic table. The Japanese guides' shorthand — 「行動速度や攻撃力を上げるレリックを優先」, prioritise speed and attack — is about killing before you are killed, and Boost Gear at +80% party speed is the clearest expression of it.

Relics that are traps, by design Some pickups are drawbacks wearing a relic's clothes. 沈黒の黃時計 (Silent Cuckoo Clock) drops every enemy's attack by 100% for one action — and your own party's speed by 78%. サドンデス・ホイッスル (Sudden Death Whistle) cuts max HP by 99.9% on both sides. ネクロサークル (Necro Circle) weakens enemies 30% but stops you gaining any further relics. Read the text; a good run dies to one careless pick.

Artifacts アーティファクト

Twenty-four entries, and they are five stats × three types, plus three of those stats again as a crystal version that gives a flat number instead of a percentage. They apply inside the Maze only — that is what makes them the lowest-priority tune-up until you are stuck.

Each is per type, so an artifact only pays out for the characters of that type you actually field. A mono-type team gets the full value of one artifact track; a mixed team splits it three ways.

Type equipment タイプ装備

Four parts per type, twelve in all. Unlike artifacts these work everywhere, which is why the guides rank equipment above artifacts and just under mining. Sensor and Actuator give HP and Attack; Battery and Jet Engine give HP and Defence.

The bonus steps up in bands — levels 1–20, 21–40, 41–60, 61–80, 81–100, 101–150, 151–200, then 201+ — and a fully levelled Sensor is worth about +24% HP and +47% attack to every character of its type.

Maze Shifter threat & the Unexplored Maze 未開拓メイズ

The Unexplored Maze fixes enemies at level 200 and needs the normal Maze cleared to area 100 first. On top of that it stacks named modifiers, and the reason it feels unfair is that several of them scale you down rather than the enemy up:

Debuff the enemy rather than buff yourself With Maze Syndrome cutting your base stats by up to half, percentage buffs on your own side are being applied to a smaller number. Attack-reduction debuffs on the enemy are not, which is why the Japanese clears lean on control and attack-down rather than more damage. Crafting クラフト is available here — save it for immediately before a boss, when you know what you are short of.

Running it well

Farm the ten-step areas

Repeat the round-number area just below your deepest clear — 90, 100, 110. Skip is available there, the ore per minute is the best in the mode, and you are not risking a wipe for nothing.

100% on a boss clear, 70% on an abort

Finishing on the final boss lets you spend your whole ore stack; breaking off early only releases about 70% of it. Combined with ore not carrying over, that is a real reason to push one more boss rather than quit on a good haul.

Check the bonus roster first

Fielding flagged characters scales ore from +5% up to +20%, with +1 AP at two of them and +1 PP at four. Free income — but skip a bonus character you have not invested in; a wipe costs more than the bonus pays.

Area 101 is where teams stop working

Past 100 you need multi-target damage and real healing, a five-of-one-attribute bonus (+25% ATK, +25% HP), and equipment, artifacts, academy level, skills and modules all pushed. Commander rank is the hard ceiling, since it caps character level in here.

Floor 201 is a cliff, not a slope The reported experience is 「201になった瞬間から初戦で全滅」 — wiped on the first battle the moment you cross it. Enemy attack and defence both step up sharply. Two things change with it: a relic crafting system opens (fuse two or more relics into a new one by attribute combination, or feed relics into one relic to raise its tier), and the successful clears reported past this point are almost all single-carry compositions — one massively invested unit rather than a balanced five. Players describe reaching floor 300 that way. If you are stalled at 201 with an even team, that is the reason.

The attribute towers run on a weekly rota

Once you clear floor 50 of the general tower, four attribute-locked towers open — and each is only playable on set days. You may field only characters of that attribute, so a mono-colour roster simply cannot enter three of the four. Sunday runs all four — it is the catch-up day, and the one you least want to miss.

Days are JST, so each one begins at 20:00 UTC the previous day (22:00 the previous evening at UTC+2). Clever and Comical have no tower of their own.

バトルシミュレート Battle Simulation

  • Tower-style survival ladder, 10 floors per day per attribute tower
  • Rewards アップグレードキット — required for Academy Level, which buffs you everywhere
  • Mining level rises every 5 quests — this is why it's a daily priority
  • スペシャルライセンス on milestone stages — one source says every 10 floors, gamerch says every 5
  • Clearing floor 50 of the general tower unlocks the per-attribute towers
  • Later floors reward action speed and durability over raw damage
Build one attacker per attributeBecause each attribute gets its own tower, a mono-attribute roster stalls here. Four attackers across four attributes is the explicit advice.
Sources disagree on the mining-level cadenceOne says the mining level rises every 5 quests; gamerch says +1 per clear, with gems on top every 5. Either way the instruction is the same — clear simulate floors daily, they are your income multiplier — so it is not worth resolving before you play.
Steal a working teamWhen a floor stops you, use クリア編成確認 to look at the formations other commanders cleared it with. It shows attributes, roles and memories, and it is the fastest way to work out what the floor is actually testing.

戦術演習 Tactical Exercise

  • 5 attempts per day, and no retries — a bad run is spent
  • Score-ranked, so newcomers won't place — but the participation rewards are worth taking regardless
  • Clearing once per day satisfies a circle mission and earns circle points
  • A main source of skill-enhancement material
The community time-saverThe first run can't be skipped and watching it out takes a while. Players report that restarting the app after the battle begins still credits the rewards. Undocumented behaviour, so treat it as a convenience that may be patched, not a guarantee.
Five difficulty tiersNORMAL · HARD · EXPERT · LEGEND · ENDLESS. In ENDLESS the enemy's HP refills when you empty it and the fight continues until your team is wiped or five turns end — but your AP, PP and EX gauge do not refill with it. It is a damage-per-turn test with a hard resource budget, not a survival test, so front-load your burst instead of saving it.
Read the rotation firstThe mode cycles a small set of featured opponents. Check their attributes against the cycle above before you spend one of your five attempts — a matchup you lose halves your damage, and there is no retry to fix it.

公式MG競技 Official MG Competition

  • Unlocks at 6-37; ranked PvP against stored defence teams
  • 5 challenges per day, chosen from 5 offered opponents
  • Every battle ends after 5 turns — this is a burst format
  • Eight ranks: アイアン Iron → Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum → Diamond → Legend → ルーラー Ruler
  • Runs in seasons, each roughly two weeks
Losing is free — punch upwardA defeat does not consume an attempt. That inverts the usual advice: always open against the strongest opponent on the board, because a failed attempt costs you nothing but the time, and dropping to an easier target after a loss is still five real attempts. Do not spend your five on safe wins.

サークル対抗制圧戦 Circle vs Circle

The only entry requirement is being in a circle. Empty circles get nothing here, so join an active one — the wiki keeps a recruitment board.

  • Phase 1 前半戦 — members pick from difficulty-graded enemy formations and beat them to push the circle's 制圧率 suppression rate toward 100%
  • Phase 2 後半戦 — the whole circle chips a single shared boss down; each kill spawns a stronger one
  • Rewards scale with suppression rate and bosses felled: circle points, free gems, titles
The enemy element rotates dailyIn phase 1 the formations change attribute day by day. Bring the colour that beats today's and phase 1 is close to free; bring the wrong one and you are fighting at half damage for no reason.
Routine

The daily loop

Reset is 05:00 JST = 20:00 UTC the previous day (22:00 the previous evening at UTC+2). Tick these off; the list saves in your browser.

0 / 0
The rhythm underneath it Advance the main quest until it stops → develop characters → wait for mining to refill → repeat. Mining accrues on a timer; you get one free time-skip per day, and gems can buy up to two further accelerations of two hours each. That's a reasonable gem sink if you're actively pushing a wall, and a waste otherwise.
Economy

Gacha, and what's worth buying

Published rates

featured—0.75%

Ceiling: 200 pulls on both banner types — standard gives an exchangeable Special License, pickup guarantees the featured SSR. There is no loss-to-off-banner mechanic; the counter always delivers.

The wishlist ウィッシュリスト

On the standard banner, select up to 4 SSRs per attribute. Unselected SSRs leave the pool, concentrating the rate onto your picks — roughly 0.2475% each, about three times an unfocused rate.

Correction, from the game's own gacha text: 「基本4属性…の生徒を4人ずつと特殊2属性（コミカル・クレバー）の生徒を1人ずつウィッシュリストに設定できます」 — you get 4 slots per base attribute plus 1 each for Comical and Clever, 18 in total. An earlier revision of this manual said the two special attributes could not be listed at all, following a fan wiki. That was wrong. They can — you simply only get one slot each.

Update it constantlyOnce a character hits LR she's finished — leave her on the list and you keep pulling a maxed unit while burning pity. This is the most common ongoing mistake in the game.

Spending priorities

  • The two monthly subscriptions — an idle-reward booster and a student-acquisition pass. Their accumulated points exchange for the スタイルカード選択ボックス【特殊2属性】, which supplies limit-break material for the very-low-rate Clever and Comical characters. That box is the reason to subscribe.
  • スペシャルライセンス — collect them free, never buy them. Fifty spent give a guaranteed SSR of that attribute, but a random one: a single limit break's worth, most likely of someone you don't want. They accumulate on their own from Battle Simulation stage clears and as the 80-point weekly mission reward, so take those. Converting standard-gacha points into them is the inefficient route and is not comparable to the style-card box.
  • Mining acceleration — situationally fine when pushing a wall

Your opening pulls

Roughly 40 pulls at the start — about 10 from tickets plus 30 from gems. Spend tickets on the standard banner.

Chase permanent-pool characters, not limited onesBecause the game is built around limit breaks, a limited character you can never duplicate is worth less than a permanent one you can. One guide cites limited rates as low as 0.02% for certain characters — a figure I could not corroborate elsewhere, so treat the exact number sceptically while taking the strategic point seriously.
Where sources disagree On off-banner SSR rates during a pickup, one source gives 0.17% per non-featured SSR while another describes standard-banner odds as 0.25%. These may be measuring different things — per-character versus per-group, or different banner generations. The 4% SSR total and the 200-pull ceiling are consistent everywhere and are the numbers worth planning around.
Progression

The three walls

Every beginner guide names the same three. They are not subtle difficulty curves — they are step changes, and each needs a different answer.

1-8
The first shock
Enemy strength changes abruptly and a starting party can wipe outright. The fix: bring an attribute-advantaged unit (Smart/blue works here) and let idle rewards carry you a few levels before retrying. This one is a patience wall, not a roster wall.
1-15
The defence wall
A dinosaur-like boss with DEF above 1,000. At 700–800 ATK you literally deal 1 damage per hit. Spreading levels doesn't help — concentrate everything into one attacker until she reaches roughly 1,700 ATK and punch a single hole through.
2-18
The even-development wall
Front-row enemy MGs hit hard enough to one-shot your units. The previous answer inverts: here you need every character raised evenly, not one carry. Guides warn this can stall you for a day or more.
General "I can't win" checklist In order of effort-to-payoff: unify your party's attribute (up to +25%/+25%) → fix anyone in the wrong row (−5% each) → raise the five Level-Link carriers → run Maze Exploration for tune-up → raise affinity on your main five → check Academy Level upgrades from Battle Simulation kits.
94 cards · 3 contexts

Tier board

gamerch publishes three separate tier lists — one overall, one for Maze Exploration, one for Tactical Exercise — and a card can sit two tiers apart between them. Switch contexts with the tabs; every card carries small badges showing where it lands on the other two lists, so you can spot the specialists at a glance.

Inflicts

Badges: O overall · M maze · T tactical, each showing that card’s tier there — greyed when the list does not rank it. ★ marks a card with a written analysis. Click any card to open it in a floating preview; Esc or a click outside closes it. The Inflicts filter reads the status table, which records ailments per character rather than per card, so it returns every card belonging to a character listed as a source of that effect.

This board ranks cards, not characters — and that is not a technicality 周年七彩 (Anniversary Nanairo) is SS. The plain 鳴滝七彩 you actually own is B. They share a name, a portrait and nothing else that matters. Before applying any rank to a unit in your box, match the epithet, not the face. Seasonal and anniversary cards are marked with a gold chip here for exactly that reason.
Two things about this board that are worth knowing Where gamerch and the game disagree, the game wins. gamerch publishes attribute and role columns, and spot-checks against in-game badges found several that do not match — the base リリー・ラヴォア is listed there as Cute / EN where the card reads Smart / Physical Attacker. The badges on this board do not come from gamerch: they are read out of the game's own card table, and on that particular disagreement the game agrees with the card in your box. Only the tier placements are gamerch's. Three names appear twice in the same list. On the Maze list the lower of the pair is annotated 配布版 — the free distributed card. The overall and tactical lists drop that annotation but repeat the pattern, so the second entry reads as the character's low-rarity card rather than a mistake; those are marked 2nd entry and resolved to her R or SR card. In three cases gamerch has listed the same card in two rows of one table — you will see identical art and identical badges. That is the source repeating itself, not a second card.
The strongest units are the hardest to finish 榊野ヒイロ and ドロテア・カークランド top the lists, but both sit outside the four-attribute cycle, get only one wishlist slot between all Clever units and one between all Comical, and are reported at drop rates around 0.02% — so skill level 15 is effectively unreachable for most players. Treat duplicates as luck rather than a plan, and build your reliable core from permanent-pool characters you can actually stack.
Story

Which choices actually matter

重要な選択肢 — permanent

Route-affecting story branches. Irreversible. The game announces them before you commit, so you won't hit one by accident. They change main-episode progression and which CG stills you unlock — and stills can be set as your home screen, so this has a cosmetic payoff too.

Date choices — worth optimising

In 学園スポット events, one option produces デート大成功 and better affinity. The event is fixed by the character + spot pairing, and each campus has 4 spots. This is the one routine choice with a measurable best answer.

Everything else — flavour

Tweety/SNS replies and ordinary conversation. A player who tested the 2-15 choice found it only changes a later teasing line — 「親愛度とかその後のシナリオには関係なさそう」. Answer however you like.

The rule of thumb for route choices — you don't need a table kamigame's guidance is refreshingly simple: pick the option that would please the character whose route you want. In practice the game makes this easy, because the branching options usually contain her name. Wanting the める (Meru) route means consistently choosing options like 「めるに頼もう」 or 「めるが母親」. Decide your heroine first, then pattern-match on the name — that reliably steers the branch without memorising anything.
Lookup

Every date event and its 大成功 answer

All 348 documented character × spot pairings, from muvluv-girls-garden.wikiru.jp. The ◎ option is デート大成功 — +10 affinity. The other is 完了, a plain completion — +5. Options are listed in the order the game shows them, so you can match position as well as text. English is a translation for reference; match the Japanese, since that is what your screen shows.

How to use this without reading ahead The event you get is fixed by character + spot, not by the day, so a pairing always plays the same way — which is what makes a table possible at all. Four spots per campus, four events per character. Once you've dated a character at all four spots you can skip the episode outright, and a skipped date counts as 大成功 automatically — so this table matters most on the first pass through each girl, and stops mattering entirely afterwards.
Two caveats on this table 【おたすけさんぽ・イン・サマー】リディア・エルドリッジ has all four spots blank on the source wiki — nobody has filled them in yet, so it appears here marked undocumented rather than guessed. And this is a live game: new banners add cards faster than the wiki fills them, so if a character you own is missing, she is newer than 1 September 2026. Everything else was cross-checked against the wiki's own ◎/× markers, not inferred.
Provenance

Sources

Compiled 1 September 2026 from Japanese strategy wikis and player blogs. Numbers are quoted as those sources give them; disagreements and unverified figures are flagged in place above. Live games change — re-check anything you're about to spend real resources on.

33 sources · 7 revisions
Where the artwork and the card data come from Every image on this page, and every rarity / attribute / type / role value behind the tier board, was taken from an installed copy of the game client itself. The UI icons come from StreamingAssets; the card art from the client's Addressables cache; the card data from the game's own MasterData, which the client caches as LZ4-compressed MessagePack under AppData\LocalLow\KMS. Nothing here was downloaded from a website and nothing was drawn or guessed by me.
WhatSourceHow it is keyed
Card portrait360×640 card artBy card. The texture name is the six-digit card ID, so Halloween Evi and plain Evi now show their own art. 92 of the game's 93 cards have art cached; the 93rd is an unreleased card that appears on no tier list.
Rarity, attribute, type, roleMasterData card table, 93 rowsBy card ID. The enums were confirmed against the game's own school-level and profile-frame tables, then cross-checked against 17 cards documented on Japanese wikis — all 17 agree.
Card title 肩書きMasterData card tableThe Japanese is the game's string. The English beside it is my translation — these titles have no official English.
Card header colour312×640 name plateTwo colours sampled from the plate's clean band, per character. The plate also carries her romanised name, but the texture is only 640px wide and long names clip inside the asset itself, so the lettering is not used.
Attribute · role · rarity marksattribute_*, icon_role_*, rarity_*_horizontalFilename. The game calls the EN attacker intelligenceAttacker internally. An older three-way icon_character_type_* set also exists and does not match the five roles; it is not used here.
Maze iconsrelic_category_*, icon_school_level_type_*, frm_class_*, img_maze_results_*Filename. The equipment tiles are composited: the game stores the coloured frame (frm_class_*) and the item render (a 188×188 texture keyed by item ID) as separate textures and stacks them at runtime, so this page does the same. The seven relic categories are the game's own taxonomy, but which category each individual relic sits in is not in the data I can read — so the icons in the relic table are my grouping of what each relic does, not the game's.
Relics, artifacts, equipment, unlock ladders, threat modifiersMasterData tables — 221 relics, 24 artifacts, 12 equipment parts, 75 unlocks, 8 modifiersValues are quoted at the highest step each entry reaches. The five-step relic ladder R→SR→SSR→UR→LR was confirmed by matching the unlock text's own (R)/(SR)/(SSR)/(UR) tags against the numeric enum.
What was left out. The client's cache also holds scene thumbnails from the adult episodes. None of those are used here — every portrait on this page is the character's card art, the same image the gacha and party screens show. It is cropped to 5:4 from the top only because that is the shape of the tile it sits in.
Which English terms here are official, and which are mine Every Japanese term paired with English in this manual was checked against the project's own translated files — static/en.json (the game's MasterData: item names, skill text, UI labels) and the 60,742-line translation memory built from the 516 professionally translated scenes. Where the official translation has a word for something, that word is used here.

The rarity ladder was corrected from ten steps to fourteen — the emblem set proved R and SR have + rungs too, so the ladder runs R · R+ · SR · SR+ · SSR · SSR+ · UR · UR+ · LR · LR+1…+5, thirteen limit breaks in all. The glance panel was rebuilt around the portrait and its tier labels shortened so they stop wrapping. Provenance, keying and two deliberate omissions are set out in the note above.
Revision 6 — 7 September 2026 · the limit-break claim, checked The limit-break section was re-verified against the game's own MasterData and rechecked against kamigame. The rule held; the presentation did not. The rarity ladder is now shown properly (SSR → SSR+ → UR → UR+ → LR → LR+1…+5, caps 160/170/180/190/200), the material costs are given as a table with the 同名 → 同属性 switch marked, the duplicate-conversion rates (50 / 5 / 1) were added, and a note states exactly which parts are confirmed by game data and which rest on a secondary source.

One error was corrected. Revision 2 claimed Clever and Comical cannot be put on the wishlist. The game's gacha description says otherwise — 「基本4属性…を4人ずつと特殊2属性（コミカル・クレバー）の生徒を1人ずつ」, so they get one slot each. The fan wiki that claim came from was wrong, and both places it appeared have been fixed.
Revision 5 — 7 September 2026 · the palette This manual is now a single dark theme — there is no light mode and no automatic switch, so it looks the same on every machine. The colours are lifted from the official マブラヴ ガールズガーデン site, read off the live page rather than guessed: its accent #0096FF (raised to #3FAAFF so it holds up on a dark ground), its ink family around #3C4346, and its periwinkle secondary #A0A9C9. The hero's faint blue grid is a nod to the key visual's background pattern. The six attribute colours are the game's own, taken from the in-game badges rather than from the website. Type was set a step larger throughout, line length capped, and the tier ramp recoloured so SS→C reads as a ranking on a dark background.
Revision 4 — 7 September 2026 The date-answer table now stays folded until you search or filter it. Terminology was audited against the official translation: Maze exploration → Maze Exploration, Tactical Exercises → Tactical Exercise, Battle Simulate → Battle Simulation, Agility → Agile as a type name, Tatsumiya Ore → Tatsumiya ore, 必中 now Sure Hit, 前衛・後衛 now carry Vanguard / Rearguard, 待ち合わせ now Meetup, and the three Memory titles are given in their official English. Character names were already coming from the official name list and all 94 checked out.
Revision 3 — 7 September 2026 The tier list was rebuilt as a tier board: gamerch's three separate rankings (overall, Maze, Tactical) as switchable contexts, all 94 ranked cards instead of the seven SS units the old panel showed, seasonal and anniversary variants labelled as such, cross-context badges on every card, and search plus a base/alt filter. Attribute and role columns were deliberately not carried over — the reason is stated in the section itself. Then, on request: card names and badges were enlarged, and clicking a card now opens a floating glance panel over the board — the way Zen Browser's Glance works — with a generated portrait, all three tier placements, the written analysis where one exists, the status effects that character is listed as inflicting, and shortcuts through to her date answers and to the status section. Esc, the close button or a click on the backdrop dismisses it.
Revision 2 — 7 September 2026, from a sweep of gamerch.com/muvluv-girls-garden Nothing already in this manual was deleted. What changed: the attribute cycle direction is now resolved and the "unverified" warning it replaced is gone; a whole status-effects section is new; Maze gained ore does not carry over, the caps-per-10-floors rule, the commander-level clamp, the bonus-character multiplier and the floor-201 cliff; the tune-up spending order was re-cut around mining first; Modes gained the attribute-tower weekday rota, 公式MG競技, the two-phase circle war and the ENDLESS rules; Affinity gained a memories subsection; Growth gained the 資金 economy loop; Special License was re-rated from "poor" to "free yes, bought no". Two new source conflicts are flagged in place rather than silently resolved — the mining-level cadence and the licence milestone interval.
